title: AI Engineer
tagline: Build products on top of large language models: agents, RAG, evals and tools.
about: AI engineers build applications powered by foundation models such as Claude. Rather than training models from scratch, you design prompts, connect models to data and tools, build agents, and, crucially, measure whether the system actually works.
It's one of the fastest-moving roles in software. Strong general engineering plus a rigorous habit of evaluation is what separates real AI products from demos.
day: Design prompts and tool definitions for model-powered features
Build retrieval pipelines over company data
Write evaluation suites and track quality over time
Ship agents that call APIs and take actions safely
Monitor cost, latency and failure modes in production

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

nodes.d: AI apps are mostly API calls plus careful handling of their inputs and outputs.

phases.title: How LLMs work
phases.goal: Understand the model well enough to predict its behaviour.

nodes.d: What training, loss, overfitting and generalisation mean, at an intuitive level.
How text becomes tokens and vectors, and how attention lets a model use context.
links: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

nodes.d: Frontier vs small models, modalities, context length, latency and cost trade-offs.
Hallucination, sensitivity to phrasing, knowledge cut-offs and why evaluation is mandatory.
Clear instructions, examples, structure and roles. The highest-leverage skill in the job.
Get JSON you can trust: schemas, validation and retries.
Let the model call your functions: search, databases, calculators, APIs.
Stream tokens for responsiveness, and design interfaces that handle uncertainty.
Prompt caching, model routing and batching.

project.d: A web app that uses an LLM with a carefully designed system prompt, structured JSON output, streaming responses and a tool (for example a dictionary or calculator).

phases.title: RAG & agents
phases.goal: Ground models in your data and let them act.

nodes.d: Find relevant text by meaning.
Chunk, index, retrieve and cite: answers grounded in your documents.
Loops where the model plans, calls tools and observes results until a goal is met.
An open standard for connecting models to tools and data sources.
Test sets, graders (code, human and model-based) and regression tracking. You can't improve what you don't measure.
Prompt injection, data leakage and guarding what agents can do.

project.d: A RAG assistant over a real documentation set, with citations, tool use, an evaluation suite of 50+ questions, and a dashboard showing accuracy, latency and cost per answer.

phases.title: Production & depth
phases.goal: Run AI systems people rely on.

nodes.d: Trace every call: prompts, tool calls, tokens, latency and feedback.
When prompting isn't enough: data preparation, fine-tuning and distillation.
Build a tiny GPT yourself to truly understand what you're using.
links: Andrej Karpathy: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

nodes.d: Bias, privacy and transparency in AI products.

interview: Design an AI feature end to end: prompt, retrieval, tools, evals, failure modes.
Debug a failing prompt or a hallucinating RAG system.
Explain embeddings, context windows and why evaluation matters.
General coding and API design questions.
